children: Zscaler reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $949.3 million, up 20% year over year, and ARR growth of 21%. The company posted a GAAP net loss of $27.4 million and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.23. Zscaler also announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by CrowdStrike and withdrew its previously issued financial guidance.
Revenue was $949.3 million, compared with $788.1 million a year earlier.
GAAP gross profit was $731.7 million, with a 77.1% gross margin; non-GAAP gross profit was $766.7 million, with an 80.8% margin.
GAAP loss from operations was $33.2 million. Non-GAAP income from operations was $230.2 million, or 24.3% of revenue.
GAAP net loss was $27.4 million, compared with $11.6 million in the prior-year quarter; non-GAAP net income was $208.4 million.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.23, compared with $0.96 a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $541.0 million and free cash flow was $416.5 million.
Zscaler entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by CrowdStrike. The company said the combination would bring together cloud, network and endpoint protection.
ARR reached $3.882 billion, up 21% year over year. Net new ARR was $111 million, up 22% when adjusted for the prior-year Red Canary acquisition contribution.
Remaining performance obligations totaled $7.287 billion as of October 31, 2026, an increase of 23% year over year.
The company highlighted growing enterprise focus on Zero Trust architecture, hiding attack surfaces and preventing lateral movement as organizations adapt to AI-related security risks.
Zscaler canceled its previously scheduled earnings call and withdrew its previously issued financial guidance following the announced transaction.

title: Zscaler Q1 Revenue Rises 20% as CrowdStrike Acquisition Agreement Announced
